ddlPhases.rule: Pre-migration: every statement that holds on a graph that still carries preserved legacy rows. Post-migration: constraints that cannot hold while legacy rows still carry the label or relationship type: uid_exists_<Label> for the legacy labels that are also stored v2 labels (legacy rows keep them until the migration relabels them to LegacyV0_<Label>) and the rel_<TYPE>_assertion_exists family (preserved legacy edges of a v2 type carry no assertionUid). Everything else is pre-migration.

markerCompatibility.fences: KsWriteFence {id: 'canonical', graphRevision, lockSeq, locked} and KsRevocationFence {id: 'canonical', generation} are singletons bootstrapped once by the migrator (ddl.json bootstrap)
markerCompatibility.migrationMarkerKeys: S8 migration batches claim KsIntentMarker {effectKey: migration:<migrationRunId>:<batchId>, planRef: <migrationRunId>} under S3's markerKey scheme: markerKey = mk-<sha256(canonical{installationId, applicationId: <migrator application id>, tenantId, effectKey})>; uniqueness is on markerKey (ks_intent_marker_key), effectKey stays indexed; the migrator must write markerKey (Enterprise existence constraint)

markers.KsIntentMarker: unique on markerKey (ks_intent_marker_key) = mk-<sha256(canonical{installationId, applicationId, tenantId, effectKey})> (S3 markerKeyOf); effectKey is the executor effect key or migration:<migrationRunId>:<batchId> for migration batches (indexed, ks_intent_marker_effect_key_lookup; no longer unique on its own); a migration batch is representable as markerKeyOf({installationId, applicationId: <migrator application id>, tenantId}, 'migration:<runId>:<batchId>'), so migrator markers share the executor's idempotence and must carry markerKey (Enterprise ks_intent_marker_key_exists); planRef = the plan ref, or the migrationRunId for migration batches (ks_intent_marker_plan_ref); persisted status applied|failed (applying is never committed; unresolved is a receipt outcome reconciled by lookup); also effectKey, scope, intentId, intentDigest, planDigest, attempts (JSON), receipt, receiptId, lastAttemptId, graphRevision; v2.2.0 (R-SV11) dispatch admission fields, written in the same apply transaction when a Knowledge Services dispatch applies the effect: markerSchemaVersion (bks-intent-marker.v2), dispatchId (index ks_intent_marker_dispatch_id), markerDigest (sha256 over canonical {payloadDigest, planDigest}; index ks_intent_marker_marker_digest), payloadDigest, boundEffectDigest, useDecisionRef, useDecisionDigest, revocationEpoch, appliedAt; a later dispatch of the same effect key never rewrites them (duplicate)
markers.KsReleaseMarker: {releaseId (unique, ks_release_marker_release_id), schemaReleaseDigest, ddlDigest, installedAt (index ks_release_marker_installed), migrationRunId} written last by the migrator after DDL and migration checks; Enterprise existence constraints on releaseId, schemaReleaseDigest, ddlDigest, installedAt
markers.KsRevocationFence: exactly one node {id: 'canonical', generation, updatedAt} (ks_revocation_fence_id; Enterprise ks_revocation_fence_generation_exists); the local revocation fence of the admission witness
markers.KsWriteFence: exactly one node {id: 'canonical', graphRevision, lockSeq, locked, lastEffectKey, lastWriterRunId, updatedAt} (ks_write_fence_id; Enterprise ks_write_fence_lock_seq_exists); every canonical write, migration batches included, takes the lock first with SET f.lockSeq = f.lockSeq + 1; graphRevision advances only when graph effects commit; locked is the executor's lock flag

readCompatibility.ddlDelta: v2.2.0 against v2.1.0: two RANGE indexes added on the operational label KsIntentMarker (ks_intent_marker_dispatch_id on dispatchId, ks_intent_marker_marker_digest on markerDigest), both idempotent CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS and not writer-required; no constraint changed; ddl.json otherwise differs only in its release binding (releaseId, schemaDigest)
readCompatibility.rule: biotech-schema-v2.2.0 adds one ReportKind enum value (STUDY_APPRAISAL) and one nullable field (useDecisionDigest) on kernel Activity and Assessment; no label, relationship type, required field, field type or existing enum value of v2.1.0 is removed or changed. schemaDigest and schemaReleaseDigest differ from v2.1.0. Readers bound to v2.1.0 keep working against a graph installed at v2.2.0 except that a Report may now carry reportKind STUDY_APPRAISAL, which a reader that switches exhaustively over ReportKind must accept (GraphQL clients treat a new output enum value as dangerous, not breaking); writers and the migrator require an exact schemaReleaseDigest match with the installed KsReleaseMarker, so a v2.1.0 writer refuses a v2.2.0 graph and a release upgrade re-stamps the marker. An incompatible change would require biotech-schema-v3.0.0.
readCompatibility.schemaReleaseDigestRule: always differs from the parent release (release.json content differs); readers accept either release when its schemaDigest equals theirs and its operational names are a superset; writers require an exact schemaReleaseDigest match
